EAST PALO ALTO CITY COUNCIL 
 
 
SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES 
 
Tuesday, July 21, 2026, 6:00 PM 
 
EPA Government Center 
 
2415 University Avenue, First Floor 
 
East Palo Alto, CA 94303 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
1. CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL 
 
Mayor Lincoln called the East Palo Alto City Council Special Meeting to order at 6:03 PM. City 
Clerk James Colin confirmed a quorum was present. 
 
Attendee Name Title Status Arrived 
Webster Lincoln Mayor Present 
Ruben Abrica Vice Mayor Present 
Carlos Romero Councilmember Present 
Mark Dinan Councilmember Present 
Martha Barragan Councilmember Present 
(Remote) 
 
 
2. APPROVAL OF THE AGENDA 
 
Motion: Mayor Lincoln moved, Councilmember Dinan seconded, to continue Item 6.2 to a 
future meeting. Motion carried unanimously (5-0). 
 
3. APPROVAL OF THE CONSENT CALENDAR 
 
Council Member Romero requested that Item 3.4 be pulled for separate discussion. The 
remainder of the consent calendar was considered together. 
 
Motion: Councilmember Dinan moved; Vice Mayor Abrica seconded to approve the Consent 
Calendar, excluding Item 3.4. Motion carried unanimously. 
 
Mayor Lincoln recused himself from Item 3.4, and Vice Mayor Abrica presided. 
 
Motion by Council Member Romero, seconded by Vice Mayor Abrica, to waive second reading 
and adopt the ordinance approving the First Amendment to the Development Agreement, with 
the modification deleting the language stating that no affordable housing unit shall be affordable 
to higher than 80% AMI households. Motion carried by roll call vote, 4-0, with Mayor Lincoln 
recused. 
 
Mayor Lincoln returned following the vote. 
 
4. CLOSED SESSION 
 
5. PUBLIC COMMENT 
 
The following speakers provided public comments: Dylan Martinez, Gail Dixon, Luis Rosas, 
Ravneel, Marianna Sumina, Mario, Cristal, Jimena, and Fatima. 
 
282

6. INFORMATIONAL REPORTS 
 
6.1 Climate Action Plan Implementation Report 
 
 Public comment by Mario and Jimena. 
 
6.2 City Council Strategic Priorities Fiscal Years (FY) 2025-27 Work Plan – 
Fourth Quarter Status Update 
 
Items moved to the next meeting. 
 
7. SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS 
 
8. POLICY AND ACTION 
8.1 Second Reading and Adoption of an Ordinance Ordering Submission to the 
Voters, and Adoption of a Resolution Calling and Requesting Consolidation of an 
Election 
 
Motion: Councilmember Dinan moved, Vice Mayor Abrica seconded, to waive second reading 
and adopt the ordinance ordering submission to the voters of a proposition authorizing up to 
$125,000,000 in general obligation bonds, and to adopt the resolution calling and requesting 
consolidation of the election and related ballot procedures. Motion carried by roll call vote, 5-0. 
 
Public comment was heard from Gail Dixon, Renee Glover, and Sharifa Wilson. 
 
 8.2 Adoption of Temporary Housing Development Incentive Program for 
Smaller Projects Ordinance 
 
Motion: Councilmember Romero moved, seconded by Vice Mayor Abrica, to reject the 
Temporary Housing Development Incentive Program for Smaller Projects Ordinance. Motion 
carried by roll call vote, 3-2, with Mayor Lincoln and Council Member Dinan opposed. 
Public comment was heard by Fili, Hunter Wang, Janelle V, Sharifa Wilson, Joseph Ocon, Mele 
K. Latu, Omowale Satterwhite, Renee Glover Chantler, Eric Perez, Ravneel, Leonel Santibanez, 
Dylan Martinez, Angelica, Sarah Hoffman, Kenia Najar, Sean Ripley, Angah Miessi, Gail Dixon, 
Laura Rubio, Maria Love, Mario, Tama Seala, and Deborah Lewis-Virges 
 
9. PUBLIC HEARINGS 
 
9.1 Water Storage Tank Siting Study 
 
Staff presented this item. No public comment. 
9.2 University Avenue Grand Corridor Project Pilot Project Contract 
Amendment 
 
Staff presented the proposed a contract amendment. Public comment was received by Stewart 
Hyland, Mia O’Brien, Mariana Sumina, Javanni Brown, Lourdes Best, and Larry Moody. 
 
Motion: Councilmember Romero moved, Vice mayor seconded to authorize the contract 
283

amendment for the pilot project. Motion failed on a 2-2 vote, with Mayor Lincoln and Council 
Member Dinan opposed and Council Member Barragan absent. 
9.3 FY2027 Transient Occupancy Tax Grants Recommendations 
Mayor Lincoln recused himself. Vice Mayor Abrica presided. 
Motion: Vice Mayor Abrica moved, and Councilmember Romero seconded, to approve the 
recommended FY2027 TOT grants and add funding of $30,000 each for Fit to the Core, East 
Palo Alto Community Archive, YCS/REPAC emergency preparedness programming, and Build 
Play Learn Labs. Motion carried unanimously among the members present. 
Public comment was heard from Melody Mchlousham and Sharifa Wilson. Jose Martinez-Luna, 
Khrisar Masann-Chavez, Teresa Fernandez, Stephanie Griffin, Lydda Sutter, Sean Ripley, 
Tracie Vanhook, Lenita, Moin Oomen, Michael Mashack, Dede, Akala Francis. 
 
10. ADJOURN CITY COUNCIL MEETING AND REVENE TO THE EAST PALO ALTO 
SANITARY DISTRICT 
 
President of the Board Ruben Abrica called the East Palo Alto Sanitary District meeting to order. 
11. EPASD CONSENT CALENDAR 
 
11.1 Cash Disbursement Report April 2026 
 
11.2 Cash Disbursement Report for May 2026 
 
Motion: Mayor Lincoln moved, seconded by Vice Mayor Abrica to approve the EPASD Consent 
Calendar. Motion carried unanimously among the members present. 
 
12. EPASD PUBLIC COMMENT 
 
13. EPASD PUBLIC HEARING 
 
13.1 Public Hearing and Approval of Previously Adopted Sewer Service Charges 
to be Collected on the San Mateo County Tax Roll for FY 2026– 27 
 
Staff presented the Sewer Service Charges. 
 
Motion: Councilmember Romero moved, and Board President Abrica seconded to adopt the 
resolution confirming the written report of charges and authorizing the charges to be submitted 
to the County Tax Collector for collection. Motion carried unanimously among the members 
present. 
 
14. ADJOURN EAST PALO ALTO SANITARY DISTRICT MEETING AND RECONVENE 
THE CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING 
 
The EPASD meeting was adjourned, and the City Council meeting was reconvened. 
 
15. COUNCIL REPORTS 
 
No reports given. 
 
16. ADJOURNMENT

Mayor Lincoln adjourned the meeting at 12:08 AM
